tone_statements.citation: van de Weijer, Jeroen, Yuhan Lin & Weiyun Wei. 2025. Hongshui He Zhuang (Baima dialect). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 55: 537-555 (Illustrations of the IPA; received 7 Nov 2023, published online 29 Sep 2025; CC-BY open access, with audio supplement).
tone_statements.quote: Zhuang is a tone language. Standard Zhuang has eight tones (Wei 2015: 33). The numeric values of tones presented below represent Chao numerals (Chao 1930). In the Hongshui He (Baima) dialect, there are also eight phonemic tones. All tone values are presented in the table below, with the pitch contours for the example words shown in Figure 15. Tones 1 to 6 are classified as smooth tones, whereas Tones 7 and 8 are checked tones, occurring exclusively with codas -p, -t, and -k. The two checked tones are further divided into two sub-categories depending on vowel length, long or short. ... T5 is the only level-tone among the smooth tones.
tone_statements.locator: p.550, section 'Prosodic features' (tone table p.550; contour discussion pp.551-552)
tone_statements.summary: Eight lexical tones on the syllable (Chao values): T1 41 (falling), T2 231 (convex, low-mid), T3 31 (falling, earlier peak than T1), T4 23 (rising to mid), T5 33 (the only level smooth tone), T6 24 (low then sharp rise to high); checked T7/T8 only on stop-final syllables, each split by vowel length: T7 long patterns with T5 (33), T7 short 45 (only purely high-register tone), T8 long 24 (with T4),…

tone_statements.citation: 李静、韦名应 [Li Jing & Wei Mingying]. 2025. 壮语东庙话双数调ʔb、ʔd的来源 [The origin of /ʔb/ and /ʔd/ in syllables with even-numbered tones in Dongmiao Zhuang]. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen 2025(5): 46-57.
tone_statements.quote: 壮语东庙话是指广西壮族自治区都安瑶族自治县东庙乡一带的壮语，属于壮语北部方言红水河土语。东应话音系如李旭练 (2011:12-19) 所描写，其声调为“阴高阳低”格局，跟北部方言多数地方一致。... 词表有两份。一是单数调例词〈45 个)... 二是双数调例词〈43 个)，目前东庙话也读前喉塞浊音声母
tone_statements.translation: Dongmiao Zhuang denotes the Zhuang spoken around Dongmiao township, Du'an Yao Autonomous County, Guangxi; it belongs to the Hongshuihe vernacular of the Northern dialect of Zhuang. The phonology of Dongmiao is as described by Li Xulian (2011:12-19); its tones show the 'yin high, yang low' pattern [odd-series tones high, even-series tones low], as in most Northern-dialect localities. ... There were two wordlists: one of odd-numbered-tone words (45) ... the other of even-numbered-tone words (43), which in present-day Dongmiao are also read with pre-glottalised voiced stop onsets.
tone_statements.locator: p.46 sec. 一 (problem statement) and p.47 sec. 二 (procedure)
tone_statements.summary: Tone categories 1-8 in the Tai odd/even (yin/yang) split, 7 and 8 checked (examples like ʔdit7 'sunlight', ʔdup8); register pattern: odd-series tones realised high, even-series low (阴高阳低); tone values themselves deferred to Li Xulian 2011:12-19; onsets ʔb/ʔd (implosives) co-occur with both tone series in Dongmiao, unlike most Zhuang where implosives pair with odd tones; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Perkins, Jeremy, Seunghun J. Lee & Julian Villegas. 2025 [online 2024]. The interaction between tone and duration in Du'an Zhuang. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 54(3): 939-973. doi:10.1017/S0025100324000239 (CC-BY).
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Acoustic study of six speakers who 'grew up in a Du'an town': 6 unchecked + 4 checked tones, rhyme duration by syllable type, consonant/vowel inventories after Zhang et al. 1999:101-102, tone descriptions after Zhang et al. 1999, Castro & Hansen 2010 and Li Xulian 2011 (Appendix A). 'stress' appears only in cross-linguistic remarks (Xhosa contour tones on stressed syllables).

sources.citation: Perkins, Jeremy, Seunghun J. Lee & Julian Villegas. 2016. An interplay between F0 and phonation in Du'an Zhuang tone. Proceedings of TAL 2016 (5th International Symposium on Tonal Aspects of Languages), 56-59. doi:10.21437/TAL.2016-12.
sources.note: Nothing. One-speaker production study showing F0 plus creaky phonation distinguish the six unchecked tones of Du'an Zhuang; no stress/accent statement.

tone.says: Acoustic study of the tone system of ONE speaker of Du'an Zhuang; six tones in unchecked syllables, two of which involve significant creakiness near the vowel midpoint, i.e. a tone contrast carried by both F0 and creaky phonation; tone pairs differing in phonation also differ in the timing of the F0 fall, and the two creaky tones differ in the timing of maximum creak. Checked-syllable tones not mentioned in the abstract. Nothing on stress.
